gql-inline-fragments-union.promptSeed:
### `query SearchFeed($term: String!): SearchResult`

## Description

In GraphQL, a `union` represents an abstract type that can return one of several distinct concrete object types without requiring them to share common fields. Because the concrete types have different shapes, clients query union fields using **inline fragments** (`... on TypeName`) and request the meta-field `__typename` to discriminate between received records.

Given the following GraphQL schema:

```graphql
union SearchResult = User | Issue | Comment

type User {
  id: ID!
  username: String!
  avatarUrl: String
}

type Issue {
  id: ID!
  title: String!
  status: String!
}

type Comment {
  id: ID!
  body: String!
  author: User!
}

type Query {
  search(term: String!): [SearchResult!]!
}
```

Write a GraphQL query document satisfying these requirements:

### Requirements

- Define an operation named `query SearchFeed` accepting a required variable `$term: String!`.
- Query the `search(term: $term)` field.
- On each search item, request:
  - `__typename` to identify the concrete return type.
  - An inline fragment `... on User` selecting `id`, `username`, and `avatarUrl`.
  - An inline fragment `... on Issue` selecting `id`, `title`, and `status`.
  - An inline fragment `... on Comment` selecting `id`, `body`, and nested `author { username }`.

testCases.description: Executes query and selects __typename on all union results
testCases.expected: returns union results with __typename discriminant

testCases.description: Selects User fields (id, username, avatarUrl) using inline fragment
testCases.expected: resolves concrete User fields

testCases.description: Selects Issue fields (id, title, status) using inline fragment
testCases.expected: resolves concrete Issue fields

testCases.description: Selects Comment fields (id, body, author.username) using inline fragment
testCases.input: ... on Comment { id body author { username } }
testCases.expected: resolves concrete Comment fields and nested author username

testCases.description: Contains inline fragments with type conditions on User, Issue, and Comment
testCases.input: ... on User, ... on Issue, ... on Comment
testCases.expected: includes type condition spreads for all three union members

gql-subscription-document.promptSeed:
### `subscription OnMessageCreated($channelId: ID!, $minPriority: Priority)`

## Description

GraphQL subscriptions allow clients to listen for real-time updates pushed from the server when events occur. A subscription document uses the `subscription` operation keyword, accepts variables to filter incoming events, and specifies the selection set for the event payload.

Given the following GraphQL schema:

```graphql
enum Priority {
  LOW
  NORMAL
  HIGH
  URGENT
}

type User {
  id: ID!
  username: String!
  status: String!
}

type Message {
  id: ID!
  content: String!
  priority: Priority!
  createdAt: String!
  author: User!
}

type Subscription {
  messageCreated(channelId: ID!, minPriority: Priority): Message!
}
```

Write a GraphQL subscription operation document satisfying these requirements:

### Requirements

- Define an operation named `subscription OnMessageCreated` accepting two variables:
  - `$channelId: ID!` (required)
  - `$minPriority: Priority` (optional)
- Request the `messageCreated` root subscription field, passing `$channelId` and `$minPriority` to their respective arguments `(channelId: $channelId, minPriority: $minPriority)`.
- Select the following fields on the received message:
  - `id`
  - `content`
  - `priority`
  - `createdAt`
  - `author` sub-selection requesting `id`, `username`, and `status`.
